title: Entrepreneurship: Starting and Running a Small Business
scope_note: Course scope: general education for US learners, not legal, tax or financial advice. Rules, fees and platform policies change and vary by state and city; each lesson says what to check and where. All businesses and people in the questions are fictional unless a lesson names a real company.

ENT.BANK.01.title: Explain why business money belongs in a separate account

ENT.BANK.02.title: Identify documents a bank may ask for, account fees and who may sign

ENT.BANK.03.title: Tell debit cards, credit cards and payment processors apart, including when money arrives

ENT.BANK.04.title: Record owner contributions and owner withdrawals separately from sales and expenses

ENT.BANK.05.title: Match business records against the bank statement and explain differences

ENT.BOOK.01.title: Explain what bookkeeping is for and keep usable receipts

ENT.BOOK.02.title: Record transactions in a simple ledger with sensible categories

ENT.BOOK.03.title: Tell invoices from bills and accounts receivable from accounts payable

ENT.BOOK.04.title: Keep owner money moves out of sales and expenses in the records

ENT.BOOK.05.title: Tell cash-basis from accrual-basis recording in a simple example

ENT.BOOK.06.title: Tell what a profit-and-loss statement, balance sheet and cash-flow summary each show

ENT.CASE.01.title: Apply a documented early decision (learning a skill cheaply and starting with one small shop) to a new small business

ENT.CASE.02.title: Apply a documented early decision (solving a problem you have and checking that others share it) to a new business

ENT.CASE.03.title: Apply a documented test (selling before holding inventory) to a new product idea, and see its limits

ENT.CASE.04.title: Apply a documented test (a demo with a sign-up list) and tell sign-ups from paying customers

ENT.CASE.05.title: Apply a documented early decision (a customer asking for changes and placing an order) to a new business

ENT.CASE.06.title: Apply a documented early decision (starting with one product category chosen for clear reasons) to a new online business

ENT.CASH.01.title: Tell revenue, profit and cash available apart in a small example

ENT.CASH.02.title: Track when cash actually arrives and leaves, and use deposits

ENT.CASH.03.title: Size a simple cash reserve from stated monthly costs

ENT.COST.01.title: Classify costs as one-time or recurring

ENT.COST.02.title: Classify costs as fixed or variable and use them in a small total

ENT.COST.03.title: Build a small startup budget with a buffer and no missing items

ENT.CUST.01.title: Identify a specific, frequent problem that someone already spends time or money on

ENT.CUST.02.title: Describe a specific customer group instead of "everyone"

ENT.CUST.03.title: Write an offer (value proposition) that says who it is for, the problem and the result

ENT.CUST.04.title: Tell the paying customer from the user and the decision-maker

ENT.ID.01.title: Explain what an Employer Identification Number (EIN) is for and when to check whether one is needed

ENT.ID.02.title: Recognize the official free EIN application and unnecessary third-party charges

ENT.ID.03.title: Tell an EIN, a state tax account and a business registration apart, and their usual order

ENT.LEGAL.01.title: Tell a business name, a legal entity and a brand apart

ENT.LEGAL.02.title: Explain that a free domain or state name approval does not grant trademark rights, and what to check

ENT.LEGAL.03.title: Describe sole proprietorships and general partnerships, including personal responsibility for debts

ENT.LEGAL.04.title: Describe LLCs and corporations at a basic level, including what limited liability does and does not do

ENT.LEGAL.05.title: Separate an entity's legal form from how it is taxed

ENT.LEGAL.06.title: Order the conceptual steps of forming an LLC and explain the registered agent's role

ENT.LEGAL.07.title: Identify what a written agreement among owners should cover

ENT.LEGAL.08.title: Explain when a trade name (DBA) filing is used and what it does not do

ENT.LEGAL.09.title: Recognize how personal guarantees and personal actions can bypass limited liability

ENT.LEGAL.10.title: Identify which local, state or industry permissions to check for an activity and location

ENT.LEGAL.11.title: Decide when a question needs an attorney, accountant or other professional, and prepare for the meeting

ENT.MAIL.01.title: Tell a mailing address, a physical business address and a registered-agent address apart

ENT.MAIL.02.title: Compare a PO Box, a private mailbox and the PO Box street-addressing option

ENT.MAIL.03.title: Check which address a bank, state, platform or carrier will accept instead of assuming they are interchangeable

ENT.MAIL.04.title: Plan pickup access, forwarding or scanning, renewals and important notices for a business mailbox

ENT.MAIL.05.title: Separate business contact channels from personal ones and keep them reachable

ENT.MKT.01.title: Choose a marketing channel by where the stated customers already are

ENT.MKT.02.title: Write marketing that is useful, consistent and ends with a clear next action

ENT.MKT.03.title: Build an email list with permission and honor unsubscribe requests

ENT.MKT.04.title: Plan local outreach and referral relationships that help both sides

ENT.MKT.05.title: Use real testimonials with permission and ask for honest reviews

ENT.MKT.06.title: Recognize when a paid or affiliate relationship must be disclosed clearly

ENT.PAY.01.title: Write or judge a quote that states the work, price and what is not included

ENT.PAY.02.title: Read and set payment terms, due dates and deposits

ENT.PAY.03.title: Write clear cancellation and refund terms and apply them consistently

ENT.PAY.04.title: Handle a request for extra work with a written change and new price

ENT.PAY.05.title: Explain recurring billing terms customers need to see and how cancellations work

ENT.PAY.06.title: Explain a chargeback and gather evidence to respond

ENT.PAY.07.title: Spot fraud signals in invoices, overpayments and changed payment details

ENT.PAY.08.title: Read supplier terms and tell customers about delays early and honestly

ENT.PRICE.01.title: Find cost per item and profit per item from a stated price

ENT.PRICE.02.title: Compute markup and margin and explain why they differ

ENT.PRICE.03.title: Find a break-even quantity from fixed costs and profit per item

ENT.PRICE.04.title: Include a stated processing fee when finding what a sale brings in

ENT.PRICE.05.title: Find the effect of refunds and discounts on revenue and profit

ENT.PRICE.06.title: Include the owner's time and limited capacity when judging a price

ENT.PRICE.07.title: Decide when a price needs review from stated costs, demand and capacity, and communicate a change

ENT.START.01.title: Describe a business as solving a problem for customers who pay, and tell revenue-seeking activity from a hobby

ENT.START.02.title: Compare a side business with a full-time business by time, income needs and risk

ENT.START.03.title: Classify a business idea as a service, physical product, digital product or content business, and name what each needs

ENT.TAX.01.title: Tell a tax deduction from a tax credit, and explain that a deduction does not make a purchase free

ENT.TAX.02.title: Separate business and personal use of an item or account

ENT.TAX.03.title: Tell sales tax (collected from customers where required) from income tax (on profit)

ENT.TAX.04.title: Explain the ideas of self-employment tax and paying estimated tax during the year

ENT.TAX.05.title: Set aside a stated share of profit for taxes using an assumed rate

ENT.TAX.06.title: Keep records for the needed period, recognize payment-reporting forms as a concept, and know when to ask a tax professional

ENT.TEST.01.title: Plan interview questions about what people already do rather than what they say they would do

ENT.TEST.02.title: Recognize and rewrite leading or yes-pushing interview questions

ENT.TEST.03.title: Identify direct competitors and the other ways customers solve the problem today

ENT.TEST.04.title: Choose a small, cheap test that answers one question about demand

ENT.TEST.05.title: Rank evidence of demand, with payments and pre-orders above opinions

ENT.TEST.06.title: Explain why likes, follows and compliments are weak demand signals

ENT.TEST.07.title: Decide from stated test results whether to continue, change or stop an idea

ENT.WEB.01.title: Make a page say what is offered, for whom and what to do next

ENT.WEB.02.title: Choose truthful trust signals and the policies and answers a visitor needs

ENT.WEB.03.title: Make pages readable on phones and forms usable by more people

ENT.WEB.04.title: Tell a domain, hosting and a website builder apart, and keep ownership, renewals and recovery access

ENT.WEB.05.title: Check HTTPS, test links, forms and checkout, and keep backups

ENT.WEB.06.title: Improve how search engines and people understand a page, without promised rankings

ENT.WEB.07.title: Choose measures that match a site's goal, such as inquiries or sales
